title: Plane: Ancient Planes You Can Visit
meta_description: Planes with the species left open. The Platane de Préty, planted in 1801 at a Burgundy crossroads, has been a protected natural monument since 1909.
intro: These planes carry only their genus, Platanus, because whichever register or record named them stopped there or the sources disagree: planes hybridise readily and the parents can be hard to call from bark and leaf alone. The Platane de Préty went into a mound beside the village church in 1801, in place of an elm under which justice had been dispensed, to mark priests returning after the Revolution; never pollarded, it is 34 metres tall, and France protected it in 1909. In Pisa, two sources looked at the plane of the Scuola Botanica and named two different species. The Hague's Plane of Park Hoekenburg grows over Forum Hadriani, a Roman port town. Bratislava's is 6.11 metres round, and Budapest's at Jászai Mari Square kept growing after the bridge beside it was blown up in the war. If you can tell an Oriental from a London plane, tell us.
